standardOnBackground  Checked by plugin
Apply colour variables to your component

Apply colour variables instead of raw values to each part of your component.



Select the token variables from the property panel.



Colour variables in the Foundations collection are grouped by colour application (e.g. interaction states, functional, etc) so that you can always use the correct token for each design case.


warning  Best practice
Use colours consistently

Make sure you always use colours consistently across your components.



Ideally, when designing a specific state of a component, ensure that every part or item of that component uses variables of the same state.



Interactive components with background colour changes in states, such as the ‘Accordion’ component, should use colour tokens of the same state for the background, but the default colour token for text, irrespective of the component state.



Components with interactive text but no background colour changes in states, such as the ‘Link’ component, should use colour tokens of the same state for text.


savings  Mandatory rule
How to apply colour schemes

How to start

Always begin by applying a background colour token to your component. This ensures that the component will be styled according to a specific mode and colour scheme.


Styling your component

When styling a component, colour values default to the neutral scheme. This means that the component will follow the overall mode set for the app and adjust to light and dark modes accordingly.


Styling your component on a specific colour scheme


To style your component based on a specific colour scheme:

Go to the ‘Appearance’ panel.
Select the desired scheme (white, black, magenta, secondary).

How to use a secondary scheme

If you select 'secondary' from the ‘.scheme’ menu, you need to go back to the 'Appearance' menu and choose the desired secondary scheme from the ‘.secondary’ menu.


When to use a secondary scheme appearance

Provide a component by default in the secondary scheme only if you are certain that the component will consistently follow that scheme.


How to apply multiple schemes

If a component will be presented in various schemes, create the component under the default scheme (neutral), and then apply the intended schemes to the component instances used in the final design screen.


savings  Mandatory rule
How to apply colour scheme restrictions

If you want to use a component only in certain color schemes, you can restrict it to appear only in the desired ones.


Apply restrictions to the original component variant and not to instances.

Select the component
Go to the ‘Layer’ panel and select ‘Change variable mode’
Select ‘_restricted’ from the contextual menu
Select the desired scheme
